title: ISSN Position Stand: Nutrient Timing (Kerksick et al. 2017)
content: Kerksick CM et al., Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition 2017 — Total daily energy and macronutrient intake is the primary determinant of body-composition and performance outcomes; nutrient TIMING provides a secondary, generally smaller effect on top of that. Distributing protein intake across 3-6 meals/day, each with roughly 0.25-0.4 g/kg (commonly cited as ~20-40g per meal for most adults), can help maximize muscle protein synthesis across the day — this is a practical distribution strategy, not a strict requirement with a narrow effective window.

title: ISSN Position Stand: Nutrient Timing (Kerksick et al. 2017)
content: ISSN Nutrient Timing 2017 — The historical idea of a narrow post-exercise 'anabolic window' that must be hit within minutes is now considered overstated for most training contexts; what matters most is meeting total daily protein/energy needs, with peri-workout nutrition offering incremental, not decisive, benefit for typical recreational and intermediate trainees.
